report.rule: Picks are ranked by the lowest win rate the past record supports for picks like them: the Wilson 95% lower bound of the past win rate of the same market's picks in the same probability band (from the threshold the pick reaches to the next one), or, when that band has fewer than 30 settled picks, of all picks at the highest threshold it reaches that has enough. Winner and regulation three-way use the primary model's saved walk-forward history (past seasons); line markets use this season's canonical picks settled before the date (their history was settled at the model's own line). Ties: the higher model probability. Picks without enough past evidence are listed but not ranked. A rank is about how often picks like this have won, not about value: compare with the market's probability for the same pick. A pick is shown as a best pick only when that lower bound is above 50% (picks like it have won more often than not) and its market has shown skill against the bookmaker's line (spread, total and team-total estimates have not).
